newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SAVES ITALY AGAINST GEORGIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SAVES ITALY AGAINST GEORGIA.

text.p: Striker Fabrizio Ravanelli, a local-born hero, delighted his home town and rescued Italy on Wednesday with the goal that gave his country a hard-fought 1-0 win over Georgia in a World Cup qualifier.
The result left Italy with a maximum six points from their two matches in European group two but with their toughest opponents England and Poland still to come.

Beleaguered Italian coach Arrigo Sacchi, his job under pressure as never before after a disappointing 3-1 win against lowly Moldova last week, could draw little succour from the scoreline that left a huge question mark over his future.

Former federation head Antonio Matarrese, who lost his job after Italy's poor performance at the Euro 96 championship last summer, warned before the match that Sacchi needed a decisive win to keep the axe from swinging ever closer to him.
"Undoubtedly he is at risk tonight," he warned. "And if clear signs do not emerge..."
Sacchi said Georgia was Italy's first real match of the qualifying campaign and he noticed a marked decline in the level of fitness of several of his key players.
"We managed to close them down in the first half but in the second we suffered," he said, with the uncomfortable smile of a man facing a media onslaught in the morning.
Ravanelli, whom he hugged afterwards, escaped blame.

The locals, for whom the silver-haired Ravanelli has remained a favourite ever since he helped Perugia win promotion to the Italian third division in 1988, were delighted when the Middlesbrough player headed home in the 42nd minute.
Ravanelli, currently the top scorer in the English premier league, crashed in a header after first half substitute Gianfranco Zola crossed into the goalmouth.
The striker, who has now scored eight goals for Italy, immediately pulled his shirt over his head in his trademark celebration for the fans.

As the second half wore on, with Italy enjoying most possession but only rarely threatening the Georgian goal, Sacchi appeared increasingly nervous on the touchline as the fans began to whistle their disapproval.

Georgia, as expected from a talented but underrated team that has only ever won or lost its past international matches, had their chances and were perhaps unlucky not to have left Italy with a historic first draw.

They hit the post in the first half and midfielder Temur Ketsbaya had the best chance 10 minutes from the end when he chested the ball down cleanly and then neatly sidestepped defender Alessandro Nesta to slip into the area unmarked.
Italian goalkeeper Francesco Toldo was forced into a desperate lunge to keep his shot out.
Toldo also dived at full-stretch to save a last-gasp volley in the area from midfielder Georgy Nemesadze.
Striker Pierluigi Casiraghi -- forming a two-prong attack with Ravanelli -- missed several chances in the second half but forced some good saves from Georgia's Irakly Zoidze.
Teams:

Italy - 1-Francesco Toldo, 2-Gianluca Pessotto, 3-Paolo Maldini, 4-Alessandro Nesta, 5-Ciro Ferrara, 6-Amedeo Carboni (18-Gianfranco Zola, 16th minute), 7-Angelo Di Livio (13-Christian Panucci, 81st), 8-Antonio Conte (16-Dino Baggio, 59th), 10-Roberto Di Matteo, 9-Pierluigi Casiraghi, 11-Fabrizio Ravanelli.

Georgia - 1-Irakly Zoidze, 2-Nugzar Lobzhanidze, 3-Kakhi Tskhadadze, 4-Murtaz Shelia, 14-Dmitry Kudinov (17-Gela Inalishvili, 46th), 6-Kakhi Gogichaishvili, 7-Georgy Nemesadze, 5-Levan Kobiashvili, 8-Gocha Gogrichiani (15-Revaz Arveladze, 29th) 9-Temur Ketsbaya, 10-Georgy Kinkladze.
